title: Isosceles-free sets in the kagome grid
statement: Let the kagome grid K_N be the points (a, b) of the triangular grid T_N (the points a + b w, w = e^(i pi/3), a, b >= 0, a + b <= N - 1) with a and b not both even. Removing the sublattice 2Z[w] from the triangular lattice leaves the kagome lattice (corner-sharing triangles, four unit bonds at every site); the squared distance is da^2 + da db + db^2. Determine the largest number of points of the kagome grid K_N such that no point is equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included: no point is the midpoint of two others), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 11; the headline cell is N = 13: find 15 or more such points of the region of side 13 (an upper bound is 40).
submission: Text file: one point 'a b' per line, a point of the region of side 13 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 14 points of the region of side 13 with no point equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is isosceles-free when no point of it is equidistant from two others: no three of its points form an isosceles triangle, counting the flat case of a point midway between two others. For the n x n square grid the largest such sets have become a test bed for machine-assisted constructions: PatternBoost (Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson, 2024) and AlphaEvolve (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 2025) found sets of 108 to 112 points in the 64 x 64 grid, the first values are OEIS A271907, and the best lower bound proved, of order n sqrt(log log n / log n) (arXiv:2610.04194, 2026), is far from the subquadratic upper bounds (the grid question is Erdos problem #1207). The kagome lattice (corner-sharing triangles; the lattice of the frustrated kagome antiferromagnets) keeps three quarters of the triangular lattice, with its unit equilateral triangles; the isosceles-free sets of the kagome grid are among those of the triangular grid. How fast they grow is open.
references: F. Charton, J. S. Ellenberg, A. Z. Wagner, G. Williamson, PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI, arXiv:2411.00566 (2024)
B. Georgiev, J. Gomez-Serrano, T. Tao, A. Z. Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale, arXiv:2511.02864 (2025)
Sparse coloring for isosceles-free grids: an AI-assisted proof case study, arXiv:2610.04194 (2026)
OEIS A271907 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: isosceles-free subsets are studied for the n x n square grid (OEIS A271907, PatternBoost, AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2610.04194); no result was found for the kagome grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS.
closest: The n x n square grid (OEIS A271907; PatternBoost arXiv:2411.00566; AlphaEvolve arXiv:2511.02864; arXiv:2610.04194): the same question in another lattice.
Erdos-type questions on isosceles sets in the plane and in space: point sets in which every three points form an isosceles triangle, the opposite extreme.

baseline.text: 14 for N = 13, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/kagome-isosceles.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..11: 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, 9, 9, 11, 13 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 13: 40 (every chosen point sees the others at different distances, and no point of the region sees more than 39 different distances).
